title: Fuji: The Shape, Composition, and Spread of Demand Bursts on Robinhood Chain
abstract: arXiv:2610.35738v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Demand on blockchain-based marketplaces arrives in bursts and at a high rate. On these platforms the data are completely visible, which makes it feasible to compare the bursty demand against the usual load. The congestion manifests as an increased demand for gas, the primary resource a blockchain sells. Existing studies consider how to price the gas. The demand itself, and what it is made of during bursts, has not been measured. We measure it on Robinhood Chain, a layer-2 blockchain that quickly became a venue for trading tokenized equities and memecoins. We collected the data from every block of its first three active months and more than 50 million Uniswap swaps that occurred during bursty periods. We find that a burst trades about as many pools as a quiet period, mostly different ones, and trades them harder, on top of elevated demand that accumulated for hours. translated_title: Fuji：Robinhood Chain上需求突发的形态、构成与扩散
translated_abstract: 基于区块链的市场上的需求以突发形式且高速率到来。在这些平台上数据完全可见，这使得将突发需求与常态负载进行比较成为可能。拥塞表现为对gas需求的增加，而gas是区块链出售的主要资源。现有研究关注的是如何为gas定价，而需求本身以及突发期间需求的构成却从未被测量过。我们在Robinhood Chain上对此进行了测量——这是一条二层区块链，它迅速成为交易代币化股票和meme币的场所。我们收集了其前三个活跃月份中每个区块的数据，以及突发期间发生的超过5000万笔Uniswap交换交易。我们发现，一次突发所交易的流动性池数量与平静时期大致相当，但主要是不同的池子，且交易强度更大，同时叠加了持续数小时积累起来的高涨需求。将各次突发按其峰值对齐后，中位数峰值是……的2.5倍。
tldr: 本文首次实测了Robinhood Chain上需求突发的构成，发现突发期交易的流动性池数量与平静期相近但多为不同的池子且交易强度更高，中位峰值达到基准的2.5倍。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first measurement of the composition of demand bursts on Robinhood Chain, finding that bursts trade about as many pools as quiet periods—mostly different ones—but trade them harder, with a median peak 2.5 times the baseline.
